I can only be myself and I did my best to be myself, which is better than the other myself did. Okay. Fine. I admit I was gullible and didn't see all the red flags of their green eyes. This is what happens when you're super lonely and super myself. And that myself is on the way over as I speak. The other myself. T2. Please tell me I don't have to regal you with a Homeric ode to my space epic. There is no Dawn out here and the only rosey red fingers seen are the blisters under my thumb pads. The other myself is on the way over as I speak so I'll nix the rest of the epitaphs. T2 fell into the black hole's gravity with an occupier friend in hand a few moments before I did. Which means my time-looped alien-infected dooplerganger got a head start recovering from being a curly straw. And for that same reason also got a head start jetpacking over to me. To punch my helmet plate in. And shove that disgusting green alien occupier down my throat. I'm gaining things out here in the Stars. [[$TayAngry->SSTS]] (set: $TAYNOGO to $TAYNOGO + 1) (set: $starTay to "angry")Like me?! How am I a threat? ]}Hi, $lifeline! It's me again. When I make it home, after I kiss the earth, my cat, and my family in that order, I’ll try to find you and maybe we can finally meet each other, chat over some good queso, see some movies, you name it. If you want, of course. I know I can get pretty tiring to be around at times. Always getting into danger. But we can dial back the danger knob when we’re home. You didn’t have to rewind those times. Any of those times. You know that, right? If you decided you were done babysitting us or were too overwhelmed by us dying... you could have stopped. But... I’m glad you kept going. I wouldn’t be here if it wasn’t for that—able to look out at an Earthrise in a moment of calm before everything—and us— goes down. I’m glad to have you as a lifeline, $lifeline. More importantly I’m glad to have you as a friend. If you consider me that. If I’m just a lab rat to you then I’m still thankful for your help through this maze of space and stars. Hopefully I’ll get the cheese at the end because I’m craving it. I don’t know if you’re down there, on Earth. Or if you’re from our old universe. Or, hell, maybe any of the others—take your pick. But I think you did the best you possibly ever could have, guiding me and caring for me, out of all of them. So thanks, $lifeline. This is Cadet Taylor, and Cadet T2... Formerly of the Varia, the White Star, the Viridian, the Varia again... And now, again... Of Earth. [[...->thankyou]] (set: $complete to true)Welcome to my passage of notes for this game. I'm placing this here before //Bad Astronaut// is fully released because from the very little I know from the leaks and the passage spoilers, this game has some things that could be similar? And I want to finish this game regardless of what happens in canon because I love it and it's meaningful to me... but I also want some idk proof(?) that I made plot points up by myself or with other friends before I knew anything about the official game. So these aren't guesses about what //Bad Astronaut// is about, but are my notes for each section of my game, //So Said the Stars//. The whole story-that-will-be-the-game has been done in rp form already (except the coming home part as of 3/29 and some discussion over T2's eyes) and I'm coding it into a game, but I won't post the rp by itself. EDIT 5/30: T2ylor is finally back on earth but lo and behold I have plans to make a sequel to this storywhen I finish it if I'm still interested. https://docs.google.com/document/d/1o-HXYVJJ48MKw7UFW-eYb3yEVUb-dlWfDRTowi_R8Gw/edit?usp=sharing That's a google doc last editte in april of this outline more or less. Since this began as an rp and therefore the Lifeline had much MUCH more freedom of choice in what to say to T2ylor, I was able to let their emotional responses guide how well they listened to advice and felt about each other and the Lifeline (among other things). In a game with binary choices this is not possible so I introduced trust variables `$TayTrust` and `$T2Trust` for measuring how much they each like the Lifeline. For instance, if the Lifeline showed sympathy for T2, `$T2Trust` would increase; if the Lifeline kept being hard on T2, `$T2Trust` would decrease. While the variables only change by 1 or .5 on average (and `$TayTrust` starts at 10 as opposed to `$T2Trust` at 2), there are a few times where those numbers change drastically and the Lifeline will know that they screwed up the relationship or the character will open up more. This is relevant for late in the story where a full conversation with points and counterpoints and countercounterpoints would be... difficult... to code in a way that feels like a conversation. So whether you can convince Taylor and T2 of your decision will depend on how much each one trusts you. And it will be possible to pass that section even with an initial low trust score for each (you just have to not make a mistake). And if they both love you so much by the end you might get a fun easter egg... like... you know... a (true) story about a butt scar. The multiverse theory about the rewinds that the Lifeline for the rp came up with that I used for our rp says that whenever the Lifeline rewinds, they connect to a Taylor from another universe in a universe the exact same for all intents and purposes, but the original Taylor that died is still dead in their universe. This is a power the Lifeline has with their comms. This game keeps track of all the deaths of Taylor and T2: how they both died/became infected, whether they did make it to earth and become infected there but without communication, and how they feel about the Lifeline due to the advice leading to their occupation. Y'all I absolutely love the singular "they," both for individuals' pronouns and for general English grammar. My Taylor uses "she" and "they" and I generally use "they" to keep them gender neutral. However, I write the game without pronouns which is kinda hard in some places but it's a fun challenge (usually) just to keep it completely neutral. But in these notes I use "they." I use "T2ylor" to describe the two as a set as well as to talk about the "Taylor" they both were before the crash set this twin study into motion. In the rp, the Lifeline chose to call T2 "Taylor" and Taylor "Tay" to give T2 back a bit of their identity. I thought this was an excellent idea and it led to some heartfelt moments along with some heartwrenching moments when this naming convention was not adhered to intentionally. I wanted to add this option to the game, but felt that I couldn't convey situational name changes very well for dramatic parts AND it would be a coding nightmare. I left that discussion in "Satellite Call" as a reference to this and an excuse not to code it. <3 to Em, <3 to Sugar, and <3 to you all -PekaSairroc (Holly) 3/29/18 EDIT 5/1/18: I meant to say this earlier but after listening to a lot of songs by //Bad Astronaut// I want to rewrite some of T2's dialogue to better fit that mood. This will probably be shaped a bit by the new game. However I'm planning on writing them with more cynicalness on the loops and lack of choices in their fate. ~*~So Said the Stars~*~ ~*~Taylor and T2 exit the black hole not knowing where they are. T2 attempts to threaten Taylor with the green but freezes and coughs up (most of) their occupier. Taylor has the choice of whether to push T2 away or to keep them with them. //LAS: Parallel Lines by A-Trak// Taylor mentions the idea of a multiverse. ~*~Taylor notices a slowly incoming ship and decides to board it. Using T2's SAFER (if they saved T2), they board the depressurized powered-down ship. If they didn't save T2, Taylor attempts to lasso onto the ship with an extra tether but slams into the side, killing them. The ship seems empty and Taylor explores the ready room, galley, med bay, and the utilities room where they find the source of the depressurization-- a large hole in the hull where it was blasted by something. Taylor goes to the record room to seal it off but can also explore it (at risk of drifting out into the void) to find the crew log for the ship which surprisingly contains information about Taylor, Captain Aya, Colby, Trotter, Adair, Antoine, and the rest of the Varia crew. After sealing the ship and turning the power, air, and artificial gravity back on, Taylor sees a human figure in a spacesuit at the end of the hall. They run back to the med bay, seal the door, take a chance to check on T2, eat some "food," and rest. The Lifeline can comment on knowing that T2 is scarred from the Mg fire, which is something they shouldn't know unless they killed Taylor once during HTI, implying their knowledge of other universes and rewinds. //LAS: Lullaby from Finity's End// Taylor is chilled by the fridge horror latent in the song. ~*~The two wake up and have a meal of chicken chunks, but Taylor is startled by T2's still-green glowing eyes and drops their MRE. The Lifeline can bother T2, who's now awake, for more information about the Greens, but this causes T2 to get annoyed and not give any information. Taylor discovers that they grew an inch from spaghettification and searches the med bay for supplies, finding a few tranquilizers and sedatives like T2 used on the Viridian. Taylor goes out to face the mysterious person alone. The person has not moved from last night and is not responding to any of Taylor's shouts or movements. Taylor comments how it's like the Varia crew in the peak. They walk up to the person and discover that the person inside the suit is actually dead... and named Adair. With this coincidental information they check the flight deck to find out what might have happened with the ship and find a deceased Captain Aya and a mission log recording the final moments before the Varia's hull was breached and the entire crew suffered decompression. Taylor mulls over the existence of being in another universe than their own, but also the bittersweetness of having a ship with which to get home. Taylor returns to the med bay and does not break the Varia news to T2, who is now less reluctant to talk about the Greens. They decide to rest and recover some more. //LAS: Astronaut by Simple Plan// Taylor talks about memory and mentions the tweet by @jonnysun which foreshadows the later discussion with the Stars. ~*~After a brief time-skip, Taylor makes contact with the Lifeline again to catch them up on what's been happening. Taylor tried to keep the ship's truth hidden from T2, but was found out while placing the bodies of the crew in the crew quarters, after which they both dealt with their own dead Taylor, said some words, and sealed the door. T2 is plotting the course back home while Taylor is fixing broken utilities in the ship. Taylor remarks on how T2's eyes are still green and glowing, despite having coughed up an occupier. Taylor goes on to mention their discomfort with dealing with T2's bossiness and somewhat lack of trust in them, which the Lifeline can agree with (to not trust T2) or encourage Taylor to try to understand. The Lifeline sets up Taylor's to-do list choosing from the air filtration systems, the water reclamation system, the distress beacon, the proximity alarm, and cleaning up the labs. Taylor can fix three systems in this time period. //LAS: Guardians from Carmen Miranda's Ghost// Taylor comments how it's a grim song in light of machines blowing up while they work on fixing them. ~*~After fixing the third system a ship appears in their proximity. //They will only be aware of this if Taylor has fixed the proximity alarm.// Taylor will go to the turret by T2's orders to blow up the ship. The laser turrets take a while to restart which causes the ship to approach at a fast speed. Taylor can fasten their seatbelt and prepare for impact or try to take one last shot. Either way, the new ship crashes into the Varia. Taylor is about to leave the turret when they see that the Varia has been boarded by three green astronauts, probably a reconnaissance crew (the recon crew) who are not the marines they know. T2 panics but manages to get to the med bay and locks the door. Taylor also arrives there and asks to be let in. T2 asks for confirmation from the Lifeline that Taylor isn't infected while Taylor gets impatient to be let in. Once inside, Taylor changes the door code and the two start fighting, and end up fighting about Taylor's distrust of T2's eyes and in general while still feeling guilty about it. When T2 begins to break down, Taylor stops them and calls them "Taylor" to show that they are, no matter what happened, still themselves. The fight and resolution always happens, but will be for a slightly different initial cause depending on where Taylor was during the crash. -If Taylor was fixing the proximity alarm as the fourth system, they're injured in the crash and T2 discovers the recon crew on the flight deck monitors. They both quickly go to the med bay and also fight for similar reasons. -If Taylor was fixing the air and water system or the distress beacon as the fourth, they are knocked unconscious in the crash and are soon found by the recon crew who infects them. T2, "safe" in the med bay, remarks how they should not have trusted the Lifeline after all. -If Taylor was cleaning the labs as the fourth, the shelf of rocks falls on them and knocks them unconscious while burying them. T2 heads to the med bay since the recon crew is about to enter the lab. Taylor begins to wake up as they enter the room and must be keep quiet or else the recon crew will hear them and infect them. Taylor convenes with T2 in the med bay. //LAS: Satellite Call by Sara Bareilles// Taylor and T2 listen to the lyrics and talk about their names and determine that they'll keep "Taylor" and "T2." ~*~The next morning Taylor and T2 discuss their plans for getting rid of the Greens on the ship. T2 suggests using an EMP weapon since the Greens' hive mind works in the same way as their Q-Comm and is susceptible to electromagnetic force. When the Greens are disorganized due to lack of hive mind communication, T2ylor will take the chance to knock them all out with the sedatives they have from the med bay. T2 hints that they want to make the Greens pay once they're helpless which makes Taylor uncomfortable but the subject is changed. They need to make a dash to the labs but since T2 is still recovering, they think about carrying a weapon (a metal bedpan). If they take the bedpan, T2 throws it and the Green about to catch them trips on it and they make it to the lab. Otherwise they're caught and both are infected. Once inside Trotter's lab, T2 is about to collapse and Taylor is quickly sorting through the mess in the lab. The Lifeline has a choice on whether to tell T2 or Taylor to change the door code. If Taylor changes it, they're both safe. If T2 changes it, the recon crew enters and grabs T2 before Taylor can get them out and lock the door. Taylor feels absolutely betrayed that T2 would pretend to not be Green and help the Greens in the end. This is actually because the Greens can see through T2's eyes and found the door code this way. The next section proceeds as normal, but with Taylor becoming infected with the 120V, dying and becoming a non-living host for the Greens with the 640V and 1000V options, and needing to overuse the EMP to take care of the recon crew and T2 which destroys their comms and communications with the Lifeline (they survive the trip home, but are infected upon arrival). ~*~Once Taylor changes the door code, they find supplies around the lab to build the EMP: a capacitor rated at 500 Volts, lots of wire, and four energy sources: 120V, 450V, 640V, 1000V. While T2 winds the wire into a coil, Taylor discharges the capacitor and asks the Lifeline which energy source to use for the EMP. The correct voltage is 450V. The comms transmissions gets interrupted for a short time but they disrupt the Greens' communication and strategy and the two (barely) knock out all the Greens before coming back online. -120V causes them to face the Greens without a working EMP. The Greens grab T2 and the Lifeline can tell Taylor to run back to the lab or try to save T2. Either way, both are infected. -640V and 1000V cause Taylor to go into cardiac arrest and die, leaving T2 panicking and yelling at the Lifeline before the Greens infect them. ~*~Now that the Greens are asleep and tied up and at T2ylor's mercy, Taylor suggests that they make them walk the airlock to just get rid of them. T2, however, wants information from the Greens and is VERY EXCITED ABOUT IT. Taylor becomes uneasy as they remember that T2 had said they //enjoyed// torturing the marines on the Viridian and suggests, again and more strongly, that they should just airlock the recon crew. The Lifeline has to decide what to do. If the Lifeline tells T2 not to torture them, T2 gets upset and asks whether Taylor's stupid naive innocence is worth knowing how the Greens got off the moon, found their ship, why they're not the marines they know, where Regina is, what was up with the black hole, etc.. The Lifeline can relent here and let them do it but Taylor will get upset and storm off, not wanting to take part. The Lifeline can comfort Taylor or tell T2 to "have fun." Regardless, [Taylor is busy]. Whenever the Lifeline supports torturing them, Taylor's trust goes down and T2's trust increases. If the Lifeline comforts Taylor/apologizes, they will chat with them while T2 is getting ready and comfort them (causing the trust to neither increase or decrease). Taylor offers the LAS song during this time. If they tell T2 to "have fun," Taylor is silent that night and throughout the filler of the next scene and Taylor's trust PLUMMETS. T2, on the other hand, LOVES the Lifeline and comments on how they're a lot alike and probably faced some dark things. They also mention how Taylor just needs... a little push... to get to where they are right now. If the Lifeline is adamant about not letting T2 torture the recon crew for information, T2 is upset and kicks them a bit, but ends up drags them to the airlock to dispose of them. Afterwards they sleep in the nav chair in the flight deck and the following scene is skipped. //LAS: This is How We Walk On the Moon by José González// Taylor will not offer to listen to music if the Lifeline tells T2 to "have fun" and doesn't apologize. Taylor thanks the Lifeline for listening to music with them and talks about how there's a connection between people while sharing a song, how maybe they do have to change themselves in order to survive even though they treasure how the Greens haven't taken away their morality... yet... maybe... ~*~Once T2 is finished setting up, they realize that they need an epipen because they're impatient and don't want to wait 6-8 hours. T2 knocks on the locked med bay door and asks for one. If Taylor stormed off, Taylor will throw it at their face and slam and lock the door (T2 sleeps on the nav chair in the flight deck later). If Taylor was comforted, they will reluctantly give one to T2 but will NOT be happy about it. Back in the hallway outside the lab, T2 stabs one of the greens. Taylor and T2 realize that they could try to blow up the recon ship from the Varia's turret (which ends with them running out of time to complete the mission since the turret doesn't have the correct angle for shooting at the ship) or one of them could go to the recon ship, detach it from inside, then do a short EVA during a short clear window in the storm from one airlock to the other. T2 is panicking and debates their options of following the standard airlock cycling procedures or a silly idea from a movie. The normal procedures take time to cycle and therefore if Tay runs out of air and can't get their helmet off in the airlock, T2 won't be able to help them while it cycles. However, there is no risk of explosive decompression and it's the safest for the ship. T2's idea is to increase the artificial gravity in the Varia to try to create an artificial atmosphere in the airlock which would-- in theory-- allow the air to remain in the airlock and speed up the time it would take T2 to get in the airlock to help Taylor if they run out of air. However, it comes with risks of explosive decompression if the theory behind the plan doesn't work which would kill them both. When the Greens are disorganized due to lack of hive mind communication, T2ylor will take the chance to knock them all out with the sedatives they have from the med bay. T2 hints that they want to make the Greens pay once they're helpless which makes Taylor uncomfortable but the subject is changed. They need to make a dash to the labs but since T2 is still recovering, they think about carrying a weapon (a metal bedpan). If they take the bedpan, T2 throws it and the Green about to catch them trips on it and they make it to the lab. Otherwise they're caught and both are infected. Once inside Trotter's lab, T2 is about to collapse and Taylor is quickly sorting through the mess in the lab. The Lifeline has a choice on whether to tell T2 or Taylor to change the door code. If Taylor changes it, they're both safe. If T2 changes it, the recon crew enters and grabs T2 before Taylor can get them out and lock the door. Taylor feels absolutely betrayed that T2 would pretend to not be Green and help the Greens in the end. This is actually because the Greens can see through T2's eyes and found the door code this way. The next section proceeds as normal, but with Taylor becoming infected with the 120V, dying and becoming a non-living host for the Greens with the 640V and 1000V options, and needing to overuse the EMP to take care of the recon crew and T2 which destroys their comms and communications with the Lifeline (they survive the trip home, but are infected upon arrival). ~*~Once Taylor changes the door code, they find supplies around the lab to build the EMP: a capacitor rated at 500 Volts, lots of wire, and four energy sources: 120V, 450V, 640V, 1000V. While T2 winds the wire into a coil, Taylor discharges the capacitor and asks the Lifeline which energy source to use for the EMP. The correct voltage is 450V. The comms transmissions gets interrupted for a short time but they disrupt the Greens' communication and strategy and the two (barely) knock out all the Greens before coming back online. -120V causes them to face the Greens without a working EMP. The Greens grab T2 and the Lifeline can tell Taylor to run back to the lab or try to save T2. Either way, both are infected. -640V and 1000V cause Taylor to go into cardiac arrest and die, leaving T2 panicking and yelling at the Lifeline before the Greens infect them. ~*~Now that the Greens are asleep and tied up and at T2ylor's mercy, Taylor suggests that they make them walk the airlock to just get rid of them. T2, however, wants information from the Greens and is VERY EXCITED ABOUT IT. Taylor becomes uneasy as they remember that T2 had said they //enjoyed// torturing the marines on the Viridian and suggests, again and more strongly, that they should just airlock the recon crew. The Lifeline has to decide what to do. If the Lifeline tells T2 not to torture them, T2 gets upset and asks whether Taylor's stupid naive innocence is worth knowing how the Greens got off the moon, found their ship, why they're not the marines they know, where Regina is, what was up with the black hole, etc.. The Lifeline can relent here and let them do it but Taylor will get upset and storm off, not wanting to take part. The Lifeline can comfort Taylor or tell T2 to "have fun." Regardless, [Taylor is busy]. Whenever the Lifeline supports torturing them, Taylor's trust goes down and T2's trust increases. If the Lifeline comforts Taylor/apologizes, they will chat with them while T2 is getting ready and comfort them (causing the trust to neither increase or decrease). Taylor offers the LAS song during this time. If they tell T2 to "have fun," Taylor is silent that night and throughout the filler of the next scene and Taylor's trust PLUMMETS. T2, on the other hand, LOVES the Lifeline and comments on how they're a lot alike and probably faced some dark things. They also mention how Taylor just needs... a little push... to get to where they are right now. If the Lifeline is adamant about not letting T2 torture the recon crew for information, T2 is upset and kicks them a bit, but ends up drags them to the airlock to dispose of them. Afterwards they sleep in the nav chair in the flight deck and the following scene is skipped. //LAS: This is How We Walk On the Moon by José González// Taylor will not offer to listen to music if the Lifeline tells T2 to "have fun" and doesn't apologize. Taylor thanks the Lifeline for listening to music with them and talks about how there's a connection between people while sharing a song, how maybe they do have to change themselves in order to survive even though they treasure how the Greens haven't taken away their morality... yet... maybe... ~*~Once T2 is finished setting up, they realize that they need an epipen because they're impatient and don't want to wait 6-8 hours. T2 knocks on the locked med bay door and asks for one. If Taylor stormed off, Taylor will throw it at their face and slam and lock the door (T2 sleeps on the nav chair in the flight deck later). If Taylor was comforted, they will reluctantly give one to T2 but will NOT be happy about it. Back in the hallway outside the lab, T2 stabs one of the greens. T2 gives the Lifeline warning about what's to come and asks if they want to know everything what's happening or if they should be vague (like Alex's warning, this is kinda a trigger warning for this scene). This does not effect what happens beyond T2's (brief) descriptions. In this section, T2 focuses on the physical part while the Lifeline can choose to question the Green or tell T2 to stop (and kill it). After some questions, the Green turns their attention to T2 and tries to hypnotize them. If the Lifeline notices this happening, they can tell T2 to stop, kill them, and get out of there. T2 will and airlocks the crew before going to sleep in the nav chair. If the Lifeline does not catch it in time, T2 stops listening and removes their helmet, fully entranced and welcoming the occupier crawling out of its mouth. Green!T2 knocks on the medbay door and Taylor yells at the Lifeline about letting this get out of control, blaming them, before terminating the transmission. This Taylor still has one sedative left and is able to knock T2 out, airlock the whole group, and after a long long journey of being alone and hurt, is infected upon arrival on earth. Q&A -Q: How did they find the Varia? -A: We knew where to look. [And you lit us a guiding lamp](if the distress beacon was turned on) -Q: How did they get off the moon? -A: Time is a flat circle, didn't you say that, T2? -Q: Why aren't they the marines? -A: Because Taylor didn't specify any specific //green// dangers.... -Q: Taylor? -A: Like we said, time is a flat circle. We will conquer all, we have conquered all, we ARE all.... -Q: Why does Regina want a Taylor army? T2: how do you know about that?? -A: To conquer spacetime, of course, so everything joins us. Taylor is just a convenient vessel for this task. -Q: Why are T2's eyes still green? -A: Hmm don't want to give away all our secrets at once. -Q: Answer the question. -A: *talks about how lovely the eyes are* --------------------POINT OF NO RETURN--------------------- -Q: Make them answer the question, T2. -A: *talks about how calming they are, all the hurt T2 has suffered that the Greens have relieved, etc. etc. etc.* -Q: T2? Are you listening to me? -A: ............. ~*~Taylor and T2 wake up the next morning and chat about fun science projects they've done to break the tension of the previous evening. These projects include the Disappearing Spoon, 1500s Laptop Charger, a Homemade Laser with Edible Medium, and (not) obtaining ferrofluid from //The Phantom Menace//. They also discuss movie ideas such as a space pirate movie with solarpunk themes and oases of O2 across the universe as pit-stops for solar-surfing travelers. However they are interrupted by shipwide rattling. They go to the flight deck and discover it's from a debris storm (the proximity alarm was turned off after the crash). The debris storm is weakening the attachment of the recon ship to the Varia, but without a detachment it will shear the side of the Varia causing a hole in both sides and explosive decompression. Taylor and T2 realize that they could try to blow up the recon ship from the Varia's turret (which ends with them running out of time to complete the mission since the turret doesn't have the correct angle for shooting at the ship) or one of them could go to the recon ship, detach it from inside, then do a short EVA during a short clear window in the storm from one airlock to the other. Taylor volunteers as tribute for the EVA and gets ready while T2 talks to the Lifeline. T2 mentions that they're feeling guilty about what they did to Taylor as a Green and mentions that, although their body is still recovering from the green-extraction, they should be the one to risk their life instead. Taylor and T2 say goodbye and hug before T2 seals the pathway between the ships and Taylor begins to detach the ship. ~*~Taylor runs to the flight deck of the ship and sets everything up to detach the recon ship from the Varia. After they do so, they run to the airlock and are frustrated at it taking //so much time// to cycle and let them leave. They take a SAFER from the ready room to use on the EVA. Partway through the EVA, T2 notices a small shower of debris that wasn't caught on the original proximity scan. They try to warn Taylor but Taylor is hit by a piece. Taylor is fine, but the debris nicked their life support unit so they're quickly losing their air supply. They decide to be quiet to conserve their O2 and head to the Varia's airlock. T2 is panicking and debates their options of following the standard airlock cycling procedures or a silly idea from a movie. The normal procedures take time to cycle and therefore if Tay runs out of air and can't get their helmet off in the airlock, T2 won't be able to help them while it cycles. However, there is no risk of explosive decompression and it's the safest for the ship. T2's idea is to increase the artificial gravity in the Varia to try to create an artificial atmosphere in the airlock which would-- in theory-- allow the air to remain in the airlock and speed up the time it would take T2 to get in the airlock to help Taylor if they run out of air. However, it comes with risks of explosive decompression if the theory behind the plan doesn't work which would kill them both. T2 asks the Lifeline to choose for them since they're not thinking straight. -If T2 uses standard procedures Tay gets to the airlock before they run out of air, but doesn't have the strength/consciousness to take their helmet off while the airlock fills with air. They slowly suffocate while T2 bangs on the airlock door helplessly while waiting for it to cycle. T2 is a silent wreck after finding Taylor dead and eventually only moves again from the airlock to check out a flashing light on the flight deck which immediately cuts out their comms signal (rewind). -If T2 follows their idea of creating a Star Wars Hangar Bay, they run to the Utilities and change the gravity level. The Lifeline can tell them to calm down and set it to 3G or exaggerate and say "crank it to 11!" If the later, T2 in a panic interprets that literally, causing them to set it to 11G which near-immediately causes G-LOC and deaths for both Taylors. If 3G, T2 remarks how heavy everything feels and crawls their way back to the airlock, opening the airlock door and hoping they don't die in explosive decompression. After they don't they encourage Taylor to keep going and to take off their helmet immediately, but the lack of O2 and increased gravity cause Taylor to not be able to do so and pass out. However, since there was air in the airlock still due to the gravity, T2 can open the door to save Taylor. Referencing //The Stars My Destination//, their favorite book, Taylor comments 'He was one hundred and seventy days dying and not yet dead' as T2 drags them to the wall's O2 supply to help them recover. After they get the gravity back to normal, Taylor goes to change out of their EVA suit to pajamas. T2 thanks the Lifeline for trusting their stupid plan while also going on and on about their BILLION DOLLAR PATENT which TOTALLY BEATS TAYLOR'S MILLION DOLLAR IDEAS. When Taylor comes back, they suggest having a feast of their favorite parts of all the MREs (mostly the desserts) to celebrate both surviving and throws a pack of pajamas at T2 to change too. //LAS: Levitate by Imagine Dragons// Taylor remarks how ironic this song is after the increase in gravity and the terror of that EVA without the gravity but they both enjoy the happy song. ~*~Taylor and T2 wake up late after their feast and having not cleaned up at all. Still both in pajamas, T2 checks the escape pods and the navigation system to make sure they're still functional and on course since the Greens had access to the ship. Taylor cleans the lab and reminisces about science and goals in life, but is interrupted by rediscovering the chunk of tunguskite while putting away the EMP. Taylor muses about what the tunguskite explosion was like. //LAS: Coming Home by Falling in Reverse// Taylor talks about finally being able to go home and what a relief that will be (to contrast their latter opinion). ~*~At the end of the song/last section, T2 calls Taylor over to the flight deck to check out a flashing green light on the ship's comms. It's an incoming transmission from an unknown source that includes video transmission. The Lifeline can choose whether they should answer it since it might be an alien transmission or a distress call from a nearby ship or a message from ground control. Either due to T2ylor accepting the transmission or a system-override, the transmission comes through and Taylor and T2 are met with the mistakes the Lifeline made-- every Taylor and T2 that were infected or who made it home without lifeline-contact through all the Lifeline's rewinds are staring at them with glowing green eyes. Taylor and T2 are //panicking// because they knew nothing about the rewinds and are faced with the fact that their Lifeline had gotten them killed before. For every rewind Taylor and T2's trust goes down, for certain rewinds the trust may go down significantly. Each Infected!T2ylor says their piece to the Lifeline and to T2ylor about how they were infected and how they feel about the Lifeline and their advice. It's meant to be horrifying to both T2ylor and the Lifeline. After they all speak their piece (or there are no rewinds) and T2ylor tries in vain to reject the transmission, Regina comes in to speak with them. She congratulates them for getting this far, teaching the Greens about the multiverse, helping them expand into other universes and fully complete the Tipler Cylinder (infinitely long cylinders work if constructed between infinite universes), and... for T2 being a wonderful test subject due to their eyes. This last part is said while looking at T2 who immediately falls into her hypnosis and is virtually helpless. Regina explains a bit more about the multiverse and the Lifeline's help in creating more Taylors for the army (which the Lifeline can acknowledge they're aware of only through HTI rewind knowledge). She also comments how T2's eyes act as spies for the Greens when asked how she knew about the multiverse (she reads all the transmissions through T2 reading them). Tay tries to break T2 out of the thrall without luck because they're panicking from all this too. The Lifeline must tell Taylor to end the transmission-- either through yanking cables off the ship comms system or using the EMP to interrupt the transmission. If Taylor tries to yank off the cables, they can't and crawl out from under the nav station to T2 staring at them. T2 grabs their comms while under Regina's control while Taylor runs off to grab the EMP. If the Lifeline tells Taylor to use the EMP, T2 blocks the way while under Regina's control and grabs the comms before Taylor runs off. Regina tries to convince T2 to break Taylor's comms which would break all communication with the Lifeline. They hesitate while Regina gets more and more upset. Taylor eventually comes back with the EMP and the piece of tunguskite which they put inside the coil. They say goodbye to the Lifeline in case the EMP completely fries their comms. The signal cuts out and it's darkness.... ~*~After a while of darkness and no signal and with no [reconnecting.....], Taylor talks about the Stars. "The Stars... I can see them all.... burning, burning, burning, shining... an endless cycle of gas and dust and heat and energy and anima and life and death... but enriching more life, laying out its foundations in such a burst of light, despite the violent flash it can begin again to burn and shine, to shine and burn, to burn and shine. Every single star, from Tau Ceti to Sol to every star yet unnamed in the galaxy-- in other galaxies, in other universes, all of them-- we don't need names for them, they exist and burn and shine all their own, saying: ~*~This is so~*~ ~*~This is the way~*~ ~*~Traveller, follow the stars home, like all who did before you~*~ ~*~We are your home, twinkling and warm, where infinity awaits~*~ ~*~You are part of us forever~*~ ~*~You are here with us forever~*~ ....so said the Stars.... And I feel a hand on my shoulder again, and... a familiar voice this time... saying: Taylor! Stop! Turn it off! Drop it! Taylor!" " The tunguskite EMP falls out of their hand and they fall unconscious with burns along their arm. T2 is panicking when they reconnect with the Lifeline who can ask what happened/if everything is ok or distrust T2 due to what happened seconds before. If the Lifeline continues to distrust T2, their trust will drop severely. T2 takes Taylor to the med bay regardless of the Lifeline's feelings and begins to patch them up, discovering that their burn left scars from Taylor's fingertips to cheek connecting each freckle like a constellation (Lichtenberg figure). They comment how Taylor got the cool scars but the Lifeline can reassure T2 that theirs are cool too. In the middle of treating Taylor, T2 has a severe acute headache behind their eyes to the back of their head. It passes relatively quickly but leaves them shaken. This is from the green inside their eyes/optic nerve reconnecting to the hive mind after the EMP blast disconnected it. They will comment on how Taylor's comms are missing and will go back and find it while waiting for Taylor to wake up. ~*~T2 messages the Lifeline after Taylor wakes up. If asked, they say that their headache has completely gone away. Taylor is still sleeping and recovering but has a habit of pulling off the gauze on their scars in their sleep. T2 heads to the flight deck to run a diagnostic on the ship to see "what Taylor ruined" with the tunguskite EMP: some of the ship's lights and the main ship comms system. The lights are important to fix because they don't want to get pulled over by the space police ;P but both will take some time to fix. T2 says that Taylor is sleeping a lot but did get shocked so it's probably the recovery process.T2 doesn't want to talk about the Green Squad and Regina. The Lifeline gets the chance to wake Taylor up who will talk about how they're fine and don't quite remember what happened with the EMP but will change the subject talk about the beauty of the Stars instead. If the Lifeline doesn't wake them up they continue to sleep and the Stars gain more influence on Taylor. Throughout this section, the Stars send a few messages in binary code of star names and must be clicked to reveal the transmission text (and decoded name) underneath. //LAS: Star Star by The Frames// Taylor almost doesn't want to listen to the song and falls asleep before the end. ~*~While Taylor continues to sleep even more, T2 gives some updates on the ship. They've got the lights working again and are starting work on the ship's comms system next. T2 mentions their concern about Taylor's sleeping habits (around 12 hours plus naps), but relents how they say they're not having nightmares anymore but rather beautiful dreams. The Lifeline has a chance to talk to T2 about their nightmares which lets T2 open up more to the Lifeline and increase their trust. The Lifeline can ask T2 to wake Taylor up, who is groggy and reluctant to be awake. They say that they're fine and try to act normally, but talk a lot more than usual about space phenomenon. T2 points out this difference. If the Lifeline doesn't wake them up they continue to sleep and the Stars gain more influence on Taylor. Throughout this section, the Stars send a few messages in binary code of star names and must be clicked to reveal the transmission text (and decoded name) underneath. //LAS: Stars Beyond Stars (Vindata Remix) from Just a Gent// T2 comments how Taylor probably won't hear the music playing from their comms and complains that the last song was also about stars. ~*~T2 checks in after fixing the comms system but is extremely worried about how well it will work if it does at all. Taylor helped them a bit when they weren't sleeping for nearly 16 hours plus naps. T2 is stressed and concerned and makes this known to the Lifeline. T2 also opens up about what they saw while Taylor used the tunguskite EMP: T2 "woke up" with a headache on the ground and looked up to see Taylor shining with iridescent white light (like the description of the figure in the monastery in Bloodline). They realize that they were wrong about the "let-go" limit and that Taylor probably wasn't shocked by the EMP since they were able to drop it themselves which makes T2 very much question Taylor's sleeping habits which could possibly be explained with shock-recovery. The Lifeline can ask T2 to wake Taylor up (which would not result in a trust decrease), but either way, T2 wakes Taylor up to come to the flight deck and hang out. Throughout this section, the Stars send a few messages in binary code of star names and must be clicked to reveal the transmission text (and decoded name) underneath. //LAS: Sky Calls to Us by Doris Teur// Taylor thinks the song is absolutely beautiful and T2 is annoyed at yet another song about stars and mentions how they don't understand Taylor's sudden fascination with the Stars. ~*~s o c o m e h o m e~*~ After the previous song/section, T2 notices Taylor stargazing and remarks on how it's the same exact stars the entire trip and the same ones from at home since parallax is tragically insignificant 12ly away. Taylor gives a few non-answers to T2 and the Lifeline's questions before T2 gets upset and asks what is up with them. Reluctantly, Taylor whispers the reason to T2-- that they don't want to go home. T2 is very upset and so Taylor tries to explain why. This leads into a debate/conversation where the Lifeline needs to convince them (through both having high enough trust level variables) to go home. The Lifeline also has the option to agree with them to stay in the Stars, but T2 will still for a little while push back until they're convinced as well to agree to that option. The reasons for staying or going home are outlined below. At the end, T2ylor votes in the form of GO/NO-GO on whether to stay in the Stars or go home. If either T2 or Taylor don't trust the Lifeline's advice enough (through the trust varibles) that character will vote NO-GO and so both with stay in the Stars regardless of the other's vote (they agreed to this way of voting beforehand). For every time the Lifeline doesn't wake Taylor up in the previous sections, Taylor's trust levels decrease significantly as a result of the Stars' influence on their dreams. -Arguments for going home Seeing family, friends, and Tom again Being able to have that "boring life" Doing fun science Making parents happy having a Taylor again in their lives Running out of food/supplies (though they have some ideas about growing potatoes and being space pirates) -Arguments for staying in the Stars Dreamed their whole life of exploring the Stars (with some fun childhood examples) T2ylor is not from this particular universe so they aren't bound to it/not their exact family Their family already lost them once As terrifying as their adventure was, it's exhilarating T2 is scared of what might happen to them back on Earth-- how their family will treat them, if they'll be used as an experiment/dissected for info, etc. They could still continue to help fight the greens as protectors The Green Squad were all infected when they got home-- is that waiting for us? "Maybe... the stars are our home. The universe, all the universes, seem to want us to stay... they keep throwing everything at us so what if we stop fighting it and stay where we belong, where we wished to go all our lives?" -Near the end of the conversation the Stars begin to speak in binary, mysteriously calling either character back to "h o m e" who has passed the level of trust needed to choose GO. The Stars will also attempt to cover up the Lifeline's advice with binary messages in order to stop the Lifeline from convincing them to leave. The Lifeline can speak (in binary) to the Stars, much to T2ylor's confusion since the two don't consciously receive the Stars' messages. Taylor's scars glow throughout this scene whenever the Stars talk. -NO-GO: Taylor and T2, happy and calm with their NO-GO decision, star gaze for a bit before T2 questions exactly what Taylor saw with the tunguskite EMP. Taylor offers them to try it out themselves. T2 accepts and both say that they'll back in a minute since they can't wait to get started having a fun--for real this time-- space adventure with you. ....the signal never comes back, even after a long period of waiting. The end of this path is open ended-- I have my own ideas about what might happen in their lives, but I will never say (unless you want me to talk about the Dioscuri and St. Elmo's Fire //ad nauseam//) //LAS: Cassini, the Grand Finale by Sleeping at Last// Played during this scene. -GO: Taylor and T2, happy and calm with their GO decision, reminisce about home and their family and, if both trust levels are high enough, they will tell the story of their butt scar and their cover up. Then they laugh about it/family memories, before the Stars say ~*~c o m e b a c k~*~ and Taylor "randomly" begins sobbing and saying that they're cold. T2 takes them to get a blanket and they both make hot chocolate. //LAS: Telescope by Ok!
